formal.title: 网关停机释放租约后仍写旧收件箱快照，覆盖新进程已确认消息
formal.aliasDisposition: One author138 shutdown hypothesis, independently source-reviewed143 and old-cause compared144; Root promotes once. Original candidate packets unchanged.
formal.validation: Static Node CLI→gateway→durable queue→actual Mimi petChat/result→instance lease/persist path, independently reviewed. No product/helper/test/process/socket/worker/account/model/native/clock experiments.
formal.condition: CLI process A using a normal durable inbox has accepted a plain persistent message and is awaiting an ordinary Mimi DesktopControlClient petChat result. SIGTERM/SIGINT stops adapters/watchers; a second normal CLI B starts with the same configuration after A releases its lock, before A delivery settles. B persists and acknowledges a distinct new message while A still has its older queue snapshot.
formal.expected: The exclusive inbox lease covers every task that can still write it, so a retired owner cannot replace the new owner’s durable accepted state.
formal.actual: ChatGateway.run waits ingress runners, but pump detached process(entry) promises. queue.stop sets flags and clears timers without waiting those consumers/writes. CLI finally removes its lock marker. Mimi petChat/result does not receive CLI shutdown signal and retains its own request timer, so A can remain alive. B acquires the absent marker and writes its new entry. A process still runs withMutation→persist after await deliver, despite stopped, and atomically renames an old instance pending/completed snapshot over the same inbox without reload/CAS/lease fence.
formal.impact: B’s acknowledged item can disappear from the on-disk inbox; B still retains it in memory and a later B persist can restore it. If B exits/crashes before that restoring write, a restart cannot recover the removed item. This is a durable-state overwrite window, not a claim every overlap loses a message or that duplicate delivery alone violates at-least-once.
counterevidence: No trigger if all A consumers and writes have settled before release, or if B starts only after A can no longer write.
Different inbox/lock configurations are outside the trigger.
This does not require repeatedly stop/start the same queue object or a malformed thrown value. B is a fresh ordinary CLI instance.
Enqueue persists a plain message before queued/adapter ACK; in-flight work is detached from the ingress handler, so waiting adapter shutdown does not imply waiting delivery.
Process B memory is not erased by A’s disk rename, and a later B write can repair the snapshot. Crash/restart before repair is required for the stated durable recovery loss.
Per-instance withMutation and atomic rename serialize local writes/avoid partial files; they do not merge a second process’s accepted state or fence a released lease.
formal.deduplication: Independent144 read original C8/N22 retry order, SWC account/dedupe/spool acceptance, CHAT-R11 notification-progress rejected-load cache, archive cleanup and slow-load notes. They do not establish this exact stop→release→retired consumer snapshot overwrite cause. One bounded compound query over original5850 MD/recursive JSON-value inventory also found no exact prior in read windows; lexical/window limits retained, no exhaustive novelty claim.
formal.fixDirection: Keep inbox ownership until accepted in-flight operations and all their persistence are settled, or fence retired writers while retaining replayable state; release the single-instance lease only after that boundary.
